x.ASV: And I lifted up mine eyes, and saw, and, behold, a man with a measuring line in his hand.
x.Darby: And I lifted up mine eyes, and saw, and behold a man with a measuring line in his hand.
x.KJV: I lifted up mine eyes again, and looked, and behold a man with a measuring line in his hand.
x.YLT: And I lift up mine eyes, and look, and lo, a man, and in his hand a measuring line.

nt: The phrase **And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold** is a way that Zechariah introduces each new vision in his book. Your language may have its own way of introducing a new vision or important event in a narrative.

The expression **I lifted up my eyes** was a common expression meaning “I looked up” or “I looked intently.” If this expression does not communicate well in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I looked up]

Zechariah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [and I was surprised to see]

Zechariah is using the possessive form to describe a **rope** that is used for **measuring**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the idea behind the possessive form with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [a string for measuring]

x.ASV: Then said I, Whither goest thou? And he said unto me, To measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth thereof, and what is the length thereof.
x.Darby: And I said, Whither goest thou? And he said unto me, To measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth thereof, and what is the length thereof.
x.KJV: Then said I, Whither goest thou? And he said unto me, To measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth thereof, and what is the length thereof.
x.YLT: And I say, `Whither are thou going?' And he saith unto me, `To measure Jerusalem, to see how much is its breadth, and how much its length.'

x.ASV: And, behold, the angel that talked with me went forth, and another angel went out to meet him,
x.Darby: And behold, the angel that talked with me went forth; and another angel went forth to meet him,
x.KJV: And, behold, the angel that talked with me went forth, and another angel went out to meet him,
x.YLT: And lo, the messenger who is speaking with me is going out, and another messenger is going out to meet him,

nt: Zechariah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [And look]

The pronoun **him** refers to the angel who had been speaking with Zechariah, not to the man with the measuring line. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state that more clearly. Alternate translation: [to meet the interpreting angel]

x.ASV: and said unto him, Run, speak to this young man, saying, Jerusalem shall be inhabited as villages without walls, by reason of the multitude of men and cattle therein.
x.Darby: and said unto him, Run, speak to this young man, saying, Jerusalem shall be inhabited as towns without walls for the multitude of men and cattle therein;
x.KJV: And said unto him, Run, speak to this young man, saying, Jerusalem shall be inhabited as towns without walls for the multitude of men and cattle therein:
x.YLT: and he saith unto him, `Run, speak unto this young man, saying: Unwalled villages inhabit doth Jerusalem, From the abundance of man and beast in her midst.

nt: Here, **he** refers to the second angel, and **him** refers to the angel who had been speaking with Zechariah. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state that more clearly. Alternate translation: [And the second angel said to the first angel]
If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. For example, you could express the inner quotation as an indirect quotation.

The phrase **that young man** likely refers to the man with the measuring line from verse 1. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state that more clearly. Alternate translation: [the young man who was going to measure Jerusalem]
The word **saying** introduces a quotation. Use a natural form for introducing a quotation in your language.

The second angel is speaking of **Jerusalem** as if it would be like **open areas** without walls, meaning the city will have so many inhabitants that people will overflow beyond its walls. If this image does not communicate well in your language, you could express the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Jerusalem will be like an unwalled city]
If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the idea behind the abstract noun **multitude** in another way. Alternate translation: [the many people and animals]

The second angel is referring to all living creatures by naming two broad categories, **man** and **beast**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [people and animals of every kind]

x.ASV: For I, saith Jehovah, will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and I will be the glory in the midst of her.
x.Darby: and I, saith Jehovah, I will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her.
x.KJV: For I, saith the Lord, will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her.
x.YLT: And I--I am to her--an affirmation of Jehovah, A wall of fire round about, And for honour I am in her midst.

nt: Here, the pronoun **I** is repeated for emphasis. Yahweh is emphasizing his personal commitment to protect Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [And I, even I, will be for her]
If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the idea behind the abstract noun **declaration** in another way. Alternate translation: [Yahweh declares]

Yahweh is speaking of his protection of Jerusalem as if he were **a wall of fire all around** it, meaning he will powerfully protect the city on every side. If this image does not communicate well in your language, you could express the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a powerful defense all around]
If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the idea behind the abstract noun **glory** in another way. Alternate translation: [to show how glorious I am, I will be in her midst]
Here, **her** refers to Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state that more clearly. Alternate translation: [in the midst of Jerusalem]

x.ASV: Ho, ho, flee from the land of the north, saith Jehovah; for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heavens, saith Jehovah.
x.Darby: Ho, ho! flee from the land of the north, saith Jehovah; for I have scattered you abroad as the four winds of the heavens, saith Jehovah.
x.KJV: Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord.
x.YLT: Ho, ho, and flee from the land of the north, An affirmation of Jehovah, For, as the four winds of the heavens, I have spread you abroad, An affirmation of Jehovah.

nt: The exclamation **Woe!** is repeated for emphasis to express urgency and warning. If your language has its own way of expressing an urgent warning, you could use it here. Alternate translation: [Listen! Listen!]

Yahweh is using **the land of the north** to refer to Babylon, since the Babylonians came from the north to invade Judah. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the land of Babylon, in the north]
If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the idea behind the abstract noun **declaration** in another way. Alternate translation: [this is what Yahweh says]

Yahweh compares the way he scattered his people to the way **the four winds of the heavens** blow in every direction. If this comparison does not communicate well in your language, you could express the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have scattered you to every part of the earth]

x.ASV: Ho Zion, escape, thou that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.
x.Darby: Ho! escape, Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.
x.KJV: Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.
x.YLT: Ho, Zion, be delivered who art dwelling with the daughter of Babylon.

nt: The exclamation **Woe** expresses an urgent call. If your language has its own way of expressing an urgent call, you could use it here. Alternate translation: [Listen, Zion!]

Here, **Zion** represents the people who live in Jerusalem. Yahweh is calling the exiled people of Jerusalem to escape from Babylon. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state that plainly. Alternate translation: [you people of Zion]

Yahweh is using **the daughter of Babylon** as a common expression to refer to the people of Babylon. If this expression does not communicate well in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the people of Babylon]

x.ASV: For thus saith Jehovah of hosts: After glory hath he sent me unto the nations which plundered you; for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.
x.Darby: For thus saith Jehovah of hosts: After the glory, hath he sent me unto the nations that made you a spoil; for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.
x.KJV: For thus saith the Lord of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.
x.YLT: For thus said Jehovah of Hosts: After honour He hath sent me unto the nations who are spoiling you, For he who is coming against you, Is coming against the daughter of His eye.

nt: The phrase **For thus says Yahweh of Armies** introduces an indirect quotation of what Yahweh says. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing indirect quotations in your language.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **glory**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in order to glorify himself, he has sent me]

The pronoun **he** refers to Yahweh, while the pronoun **me** refers to the prophetic speaker. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has sent me, his prophet]

Yahweh is using **the one touching you is touching the apple of his eye** as a common expression of the culture to mean “harming you is harming what is most precious to him.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the one who harms you harms what Yahweh treasures most]

x.ASV: For, behold, I will shake my hand over them, and they shall be a spoil to those that served them; and ye shall know that Jehovah of hosts hath sent me.
x.Darby: For behold, I will shake my hand upon them, and they shall become a spoil to those that served them: and ye shall know that Jehovah of hosts hath sent me.
x.KJV: For, behold, I will shake mine hand upon them, and they shall be a spoil to their servants: and ye shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me.
x.YLT: For lo, I am waving my hand against them, And they have been a spoil to their servants. And ye have known that Jehovah of Hosts hath sent me.

nt: Zechariah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Look, I am waving my hand over them]

Here, **my hand** represents Yahweh’s power to punish. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am about to strike them with my power]

The pronoun **me** refers to the prophetic speaker. This statement is outside Yahweh’s direct speech. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh of Armies has sent me, his prophet]

x.ASV: Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion; for, lo, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith Jehovah.
x.Darby: Sing aloud and rejoice, daughter of Zion; for behold, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith Jehovah.
x.KJV: Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion: for, lo, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith the Lord.
x.YLT: Singe, and rejoice, O daughter of Zion, For lo, I am coming, and have dwelt in thy midst, An affirmation of Jehovah.

nt: The terms **Sing** and **rejoice** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Celebrate with great joy]

Yahweh is using **daughter of Zion** as a common expression of the culture to refer to the people of Jerusalem. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [people of Zion]

Zechariah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [watch]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **declaration**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [this is what Yahweh has declared]

x.ASV: And many nations shall join themselves to Jehovah in that day, and shall be my people; and I will dwell in the midst of thee, and thou shalt know that Jehovah of hosts hath sent me unto thee.
x.Darby: And many nations shall join themselves to Jehovah in that day, and shall be unto me for a people; and I will dwell in the midst of thee, and thou shalt know that Jehovah of hosts hath sent me unto thee.
x.KJV: And many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day, and shall be my people: and I will dwell in the midst of thee, and thou shalt know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me unto thee.
x.YLT: And joined have been many nations unto Jehovah in that day, And they have been to Me for a people, And I have dwelt in thy midst, And thou hast known that Jehovah of Hosts hath sent me unto thee.

nt: By **join themselves to Yahweh**, Zechariah means become worshipers of Yahweh. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And people from many nations will worship Yahweh like the Israelites]

Yahweh is using the term **day** to refer to a specific time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. See the Introduction to Zechariah for a discussion of the phrase “in that day.”

Here the pronoun **you** is singular and refers to the people of Zion, and the pronoun **me** refers to the prophetic speaker. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And you, people of Zion, will know that Yahweh of Armies has sent me, his prophet, to you]

x.ASV: And Jehovah shall inherit Judah as his portion in the holy land, and shall yet choose Jerusalem.
x.Darby: And Jehovah shall inherit Judah [as] his portion in the holy land, and shall yet choose Jerusalem.
x.KJV: And the Lord shall inherit Judah his portion in the holy land, and shall choose Jerusalem again.
x.YLT: And Jehovah hath inherited Judah, His portion on the holy ground, And He hath fixed again on Jerusalem.

nt: The word translated as **will inherit** means to take formal, permanent possession of something as one’s rightful property. It does not imply that a previous owner has died. If the word you use for **will inherit** would give your readers that wrong impression, you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [will claim Judah as his possession]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the holy land]

x.ASV: Be silent, all flesh, before Jehovah; for he is waked up out of his holy habitation.
x.Darby: Let all flesh be silent before Jehovah; for he is risen up out of his holy habitation.
x.KJV: Be silent, O all flesh, before the Lord: for he is raised up out of his holy habitation.
x.YLT: Hush, all flesh, because of Jehovah, For He hath been roused up from His holy habitation!'

nt: Zechariah is using the exclamation **Hush** to express a strong feeling of reverence and awe before Yahweh. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. If not, you could say what Zechariah was feeling. Alternate translation: [Be silent]
Here, **all flesh** represents all living people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all people]

Here, **the face of Yahweh** represents the presence of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from the presence of Yahweh]

Here Zechariah is speaking of Yahweh as if he were a person who had been sleeping and has now **been roused** to take action. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he has risen to act from his holy dwelling place]

If it would be more natural in your language, you could state **he has been roused** with an active form. The context indicates that Yahweh himself is the agent of this action. Alternate translation: [he has roused himself]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from his holy dwelling place]
